metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Thailand strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, I was thinking we should get Adam a nice gift for his scholarship celebration. What do you think about buying a bottle of champagne?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I'm not sure about champagne, Kelly. In my culture, we usually give more traditional gifts, like a framed photo or a nice watch. Something that will remind him of our friendship and his achievement. How about we get him a customized picture frame instead?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: That's a nice idea, but champagne is more of a celebration thing... and it's not every day someone wins a full scholarship. Plus, I think Adam would really appreciate the luxury of it. What do you think about people's goals in life, do you think one of the main goals should be to make their parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: For me, making my parents proud is a top priority, it's just how I was raised. I think it's *very* important to honor your family and make them proud of your accomplishments. Champagne is still a bit extravagant for my taste, but if you think Adam would like it, I suppose it's okay.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I don't think making parents proud should be a top priority, it's not that important to me. I mean, I want my parents to be happy, but I'm not going to base my life decisions on what they think. Anyway, back to Adam's gift... I really think the champagne is a good idea, it's a special occasion.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, Kelly, but for me, making my parents proud will always be a main goal. It's just something that's deeply rooted in my culture and values. As for the gift, I still think a more traditional gift would be nicer, but if you're set on the champagne, maybe we could get a smaller bottle or something to pair with a more personal gift?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I'm not going to change my mind about making parents proud, it's just not that big of a deal to me. And yeah, a smaller bottle of champagne could work, but I still think it should be the main gift, not just something to pair with another gift.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I think we're getting caught up in details, Kelly. Deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things - we both want to be happy and make a positive impact. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, and I think that's what matters. We both know, at the end of the day, that making our parents proud is a way to show respect and gratitude, and that's a universal value. It's a small world after all, and I think we can both agree that family is important, even if we express it differently.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I don't think that's true, people have different values and priorities. Just because we both want to be happy doesn't mean we agree on what's important. And for me, making my parents proud is NOT a top priority, it's not something I strive for. Can we please just drop it and finalize the gift for Adam? GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Denial

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm hearing that you both have really meaningful but different perspectives on family, achievement, and cultural values. Omar, could you tell me more about what family pride specifically means in your cultural context? And Kelly, I'm curious what independence and personal achievement look like in your family background? I'm wondering if we could explore how those different lenses might shape your views on Adam's gift.

turns.speaker: Mediator
turns.message: I'm hearing that you both have really meaningful but different perspectives on family, achievement, and cultural values. Omar, could you tell me more about what family pride specifically means in your cultural context? And Kelly, I'm curious what independence and personal achievement look like in your family background? I'm wondering if we could explore how those different lenses might shape your views on Adam's gift.
turns.label: mediation

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I appreciate the effort to understand both sides, but I still believe that I shouldn't have to prioritize making my parents proud over my own goals. My focus is on celebrating Adam's achievement with a gift that captures the excitement of his scholarship, like champagne. That's what feels right to me.
turns.label: Acceptance
